scope: Corollary 9.1 (Common independent sets) of the manuscript “Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids” (preprints/Approximate-counting-of-common-bases-of-two-matroids-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 114 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ed3dfdefcfa677a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M1, M2 be arbitrary matroids on an explicitly enumerated ground set [n], supplied by fixed exact independence oracles with n-bit subset queries. Their ranks may differ. For an integer k, let Ck consist of the k-element subsets of [n] independent in both matroids, and put C = n [ j=0 Cj, h = max I∈C |I|, Cmax = Ch. The maximum h is well defined because ∅ ∈ C. Each family F ∈ {Ck, C, Cmax} has the following algorithms. (i) Given rational ϵ, δ ∈ (0, 1), a randomized oracle algorithm returns a nonnegative rational b N satisfying P  (1 − ϵ)|F| ≤ b N ≤ (1 + ϵ)|F|  ≥ 1 − δ. If F = ∅, an exact pretest returns 0 before randomization. On every execution, oracle calls and other bit operations are bounded by a fixed polynomial in n, ℓ, ϵ−1, log δ−1. (ii) Given rational θ ∈ (0, 1), a randomized oracle algorithm decides emptiness exactly. If F = ∅, it returns a distinguished symbol ⊥. Otherwise it returns S ∈ F on every execution, and its output law satisfies dTV L(S), Unif(F)  = 1 2 X I∈F P[S = I] − 1 |F| ≤ θ. On every execution, oracle calls and other bit operations are bounded by a fixed polynomial in n, ℓ, θ−1. Here ℓ is the binary encoding length of the numerical inputs to the algorithm in question, including k only for Ck. Both algorithms use only the two given independence oracles and independent unbiased random bits.
